newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Olympics man resigns as Reef Casino chair.
newsitem.headline: Olympics man resigns as Reef Casino chair.

text.p: Troubled casino operator Reef Casino Trust said on Wednesday that chairman John Coates had resigned in order to devote more time to his role as president of the Australian Olympic Committee (AOC).
Coates is also involved with the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG) for the staging the 2000 Olympics.
Reef Casino said Ian Ferrier, senior partner of accountants Ferrier Hodgson and Co, would replace Coates as the director of the manager of the trust appointed by the AOC.
Ferrier, who specialises in company receiverships, had previously been approved by the Queensland Casino Control Board as an alternate director for Coates, Reef Casino said.

Reef Casino is currently seeking additional funds following the withdrawal last year of a A$15 million external working capital facility used to fund high-rolling gambler visits to the Reef Casino at Cairns in northern Queensland.

The AOC is not proposing that Ferrier be elected chairman of the trust, who must be one of the directors appointed by Reef Casino shareholders, the Australian Tourism Group, the AOC and the two independent directors.
"Going forward, we think it is in the best interests of the Trust and all unitholders that the chairman be one of the independent directors," Coates said.

The AOC is currently looking at a big loss on its A$7 million investment in the Reef Casino. The AOC is a founding sharholder in the casino, which has seen its units dive to current levels of 16.5 cents from around A$1.40 when it first listed on the Australian Stock Exchnage in November 1995.
Coates has come under fire for investing a large part of the AOC's funds in the Reef Casino that has consistently failed to match its own profit and revenue forecasts.
Reef Casino made a maiden half year net loss of A$9.51 million in the six months ended December 31, 1996.
Casinos Austria International Ltd owns about 13 percent of Reef Casino.
